title: Fermentation as Preservation and Alternative Food Production
shortDescription: Biopreservation, bacteriocins and the new protein sources: single-cell protein, precision fermentation, cultured meat and more.
genZNote: The next burger might be grown, not raised. Alt-protein is the future-of-food flex — know SCP, precision fermentation and cultivated meat.

sections.heading: Fermentation and Preservation
bullets: Fermentation preserves by acid (pH drop), alcohol, competition, bacteriocins (nisin — permitted food preservative; pediocin), hydrogen peroxide and reuterin.
Biopreservation: protective cultures and bacteriophages to control Listeria, Salmonella.
Examples: pickles, sauerkraut, yoghurt, fermented sausages and fish sauces; hurdle effect with salt and low aw.

sections.heading: Alternative Food Production
sections.body: Drivers: land and water pressure, climate emissions, animal welfare, food security. Challenges: cost, consumer acceptance, allergenicity, scale-up, labelling and regulatory approval — FSSAI Novel Food rules apply in India.

table.caption: Alternatives
rows: Approved in a few countries; not yet approved in India

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Fermentation extends shelf life and creates diverse foods, while alternative food-production technologies use microbes, cells and controlled environments to supply protein and nutrients sustainably.
keyFacts: Nisin is a bacteriocin from Lactococcus lactis.

commonTraps: Do not call plant-based meat "cultivated meat".

sources.name: FAO — Edible Insects and Future Foods
